solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Impressed by onset of emotional charge

parts.note: to impress a mark on something is to stamp it

indicators.note: the onset of a word is where it begins, so only its opening letter is taken

explanation.surface: Someone stirred by a rush of feeling, as if moved at the start of an emotional outburst.
explanation.definitionFit: A headlong rush of a frightened herd or crowd is a charge, used here as a noun.

clue.text: Sink second drink

parts.note: cupper is an accepted variant spelling of cuppa, a cup of tea

explanation.surface: An instruction to down a second drink.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Sink' looks like downing a drink, which suits the surface; it is the verb for wrecking a ship.
explanation.definitionFit: Deliberately scuttling a ship sends it to the bottom, and figuratively it means to wreck a plan.

clue.text: Like swallowing first of beers in six-pack?

indicators.note: one piece swallowing another takes it inside itself

parts.note: 'as' can mean like, in the way that

indicators.note: the first of a word is just its opening letter

explanation.surface: A question about whether a beer six-pack is so called for swallowing beers.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Six-pack' looks like the beer cans; it is the slang for well-defined stomach muscles.
explanation.definitionFit: A toned set of stomach muscles is nicknamed a six-pack, and those muscles are the abdominals, shortened in slang.

clue.text: Attractive, e.g. on being shot in image?

definitions.text: Attractive, e.g. on being shot in image?

indicators.note: the other pieces are set in the middle of the picture word

parts.note: a pic is a picture, an image
hot is slang for sexually attractive

indicators.note: something shot is wrecked or ruined, so these letters are jumbled

explanation.surface: Someone looking good, for instance, when being shot by a camera for a picture.
explanation.walkthrough: 'shot' suggests a gun, but here it means wrecked, the anagram signal. Read as a whole, the clue also defines the answer: looking attractive in pictures.
explanation.definitionFit: The whole clue describes someone who looks attractive whenever a camera takes a picture of them.

clue.text: Races through homework, a simple piece

indicators.note: the races run through the middle of the homework

parts.note: DIY, do-it-yourself, is home improvement work
TT, Tourist Trophy, is the Isle of Man motorcycle races

explanation.surface: A schoolchild dashing through homework to produce a simple piece of writing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Homework' is not school work but home improvement, DIY.
explanation.definitionFit: A short, unsophisticated song or verse is a simple musical or poetic piece.

clue.text: Sort out hostelry? I'm amazed about that

indicators.note: the exclamation goes about, around, the hostelry

parts.note: wow is an exclamation of amazement
an inn is a hostelry, a pub or hotel

explanation.surface: Someone asked to sort out a pub, exclaiming in astonishment at the request.
explanation.definitionFit: To separate the good from the bad, as grain from chaff, is to sort it out.

clue.text: Somewhat paranoid about where Scots live

indicators.note: about here means turned around, read the other way
somewhat of the word means only part of its letters are used

explanation.surface: A paranoid worry concerning the places Scottish people live.
explanation.definitionFit: A small Hebridean island off western Scotland, with residents who are Scottish, is one place Scots live.

clue.text: Polish cop to go AWOL, crossing river

parts.note: to cop or nail someone is to catch them

indicators.note: the vanishing act crosses, goes across, the river letter

parts.note: going absent without leave is to vanish

explanation.surface: A police officer of Polish nationality deserting by crossing a river.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Polish' looks like the nationality; it is the cosmetic for fingernails. 'Cop' is a verb, to catch.
explanation.definitionFit: Coloured lacquer painted onto fingernails is a cosmetic polish.

clue.text: Flatter, like vehicles with raised base

indicators.note: in a down entry raising a letter moves it higher, nearer the top

parts.note: vehicles move on wheels, so they are wheeled
in a down entry the base is the bottom letter, here the last D

explanation.surface: Something flatter, comparable to vehicles that have a raised underside.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Flatter' looks like a comparative adjective; it is the verb. 'raised' lifts the final D of WHEELED two places up the column.
explanation.definitionFit: To coax someone with sweet talk and praise is to flatter them into agreeing.

clue.text: Two versions of the writer's books at hand

parts.note: the writer's can be I'm (the writer is) or mine (belonging to the writer), both taken
NT is the New Testament, books of the Bible

explanation.surface: An author with two editions of their books close by.
explanation.walkthrough: 'The writer' is the crossword's way of saying I or me, the setter.
explanation.definitionFit: Something about to happen is near, close at hand in time.

clue.text: Wears effeminate clothes below the belt

indicators.note: here a verb: effeminate clothes, wraps around, the wearing word

parts.note: an effeminate man is not manlike, unmanlike
to sport an item is to wear it

explanation.surface: A man who dresses in effeminate clothes, below the belt as it were.
explanation.walkthrough: 'clothes' reads as a noun but is a verb: the effeminate word clothes, wraps around, the word for wears.
explanation.definitionFit: A boxing punch below the belt is illegal, so the idiom means unfair or ungentlemanly.

clue.text: Cypriot man's broken handle

indicators.note: something broken is in pieces, so these letters are reassembled in a new order

explanation.surface: A man from Cyprus who has broken a handle.
explanation.walkthrough: 'handle' is slang for a name, not a door handle; 's is 'is' linking the two.
explanation.definitionFit: A surname formed from a father's name is a kind of name, and handle is slang for a name.

clue.text: Alcoholic drink animated couple

definitions.meaning: a hot spiced cocktail of rum, brandy and beaten egg
the cat and mouse pair of the classic cartoon series

explanation.surface: A cocktail and the cartoon pair sharing a name.
explanation.definitionFit: A hot eggnog-style punch and the MGM cartoon cat and mouse share this two-name title.

clue.text: Classical writer of film given Oscar at first

indicators.note: says the Oscar letter comes at the start, before the film

parts.note: Oscar is O in the NATO phonetic alphabet
a vid is a video, a film

explanation.surface: An ancient author whose film adaptation won an Oscar first.
explanation.definitionFit: The Roman poet who wrote the Metamorphoses is an author of classical antiquity.

clue.text: Suppress dodgy licence, pub losing 100 litres

indicators.note: something dodgy is unreliable or crooked, so these letters are shuffled
the pooled letters lose one of their letters, the numeral named next

parts.note: C is the Roman numeral for 100

explanation.surface: A pub with a dubious licence being shut down after losing a hundred litres.
explanation.walkthrough: 'losing' takes one C (100) out of LICENCE PUB, and 'dodgy' rearranges the remaining LICENEPUB into BLUEPENCI. A blue pencil was the traditional editor's or censor's tool.
explanation.definitionFit: Editors censor text by striking it through with a blue crayon, so the phrase means to cut or suppress.

clue.text: Mike donning American cowboy's garment

indicators.note: the cowboy dons, puts on, the Mike letter, wrapping it

parts.note: in the US a cowboy who lassoes cattle is a roper
Mike is M in the NATO phonetic alphabet

explanation.surface: A man called Mike putting on an American cowboy's clothing.
explanation.walkthrough: A wordplay that makes a plural answers a singular 'garment': rompers is one item, like trousers.
explanation.definitionFit: A one-piece playsuit worn by small children is a garment, singular despite the plural form.

clue.text: Copy what used to be your secret

parts.note: to steal an idea is to copy it
thy is the old form of your

explanation.surface: Copying what you once had, kept secret.
explanation.definitionFit: Done furtively and quietly so as not to be noticed is secret in manner.

clue.text: Blow up general engaging in manoeuvres

indicators.note: an army on manoeuvres moves about, so the general's letters are moved around

explanation.surface: A military commander made bigger, taking part in military exercises.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Blow up' suggests explosions to fit the army; it means to make bigger, as with a photograph.
explanation.definitionFit: To blow up a photo is to make it bigger, the photographic sense of magnify.

clue.text: The writer's twice musing

parts.note: a pen is a writer, so the writer's is pen's
the writer's read a second time, as I've, the writer has

explanation.surface: An author, twice over, lost in thought.
explanation.walkthrough: 'twice' tells you to read 'The writer's' two ways: pen's (belonging to a pen) and I've (I have).
explanation.definitionFit: Being deep in thought, reflective, is musing used as an adjective.

clue.text: Do like to put in some defensive work

indicators.note: the imitation is put in the middle of the word for some

parts.note: part means some of something
to ape someone is to do as they do, to imitate

explanation.surface: An instruction to copy someone in carrying out some fortification.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Do' looks like a party or a verb on its own; 'Do like' together means imitate.
explanation.definitionFit: A protective wall along a rampart or roof is a fortification, a defensive work.

clue.text: Awful drivers may stop here

definitions.meaning: racing drivers stop at trackside service bays during a race

explanation.surface: A dreadful place where motorists might pull up.
explanation.definitionFit: Slang for the very worst, and also the motor-racing service area where cars refuel and change tyres.

clue.text: Dispenser of liquid sulphur supported by petition

indicators.note: in a down entry the supporting word sits below, so the sulphur letter comes on top

parts.note: S is the chemical symbol for sulphur
a prayer is a petition, a humble request

explanation.surface: A device spraying sulphur, with a petition backing it.
explanation.definitionFit: A device that ejects liquid in fine droplets is a dispenser of it.

clue.text: Eastern ruler open to the west

indicators.note: in an across entry west is leftward, so the word is written backwards

parts.note: a door ajar is slightly open

explanation.surface: An oriental monarch willing to open up to Western influence.
explanation.definitionFit: An Indian king or prince is a ruler in the East.

clue.text: Wholly good air introduced by singer

indicators.note: the singer comes first, introducing the other pieces

parts.note: an alto is a singer with a low female or high male voice
the ether is the upper air, the sky

explanation.surface: A wonderful tune presented by a vocalist.
explanation.walkthrough: 'air' looks like a tune to suit the singer; it is the ether, the sky.
explanation.definitionFit: Completely, entirely, is wholly as an adverb.

clue.text: Wrong note gives beat

parts.note: a guess that is out is wrong
do (doh) is a note of the sol-fa scale

explanation.surface: A musician's wrong note throwing off the beat.
explanation.walkthrough: 'beat' sounds musical but means defeat, surpass.
explanation.definitionFit: To surpass or do better than a rival is to beat them.

clue.text: Before Norman's denial, answer shortly

indicators.note: the answer letter is placed before the denial

parts.note: the Normans spoke French, and non is no in French

explanation.surface: Someone answering briefly after a Norman says no.
explanation.definitionFit: An archaic word for soon, in a little while, which is shortly.

clue.text: Sadly banking most of payment (like this)

indicators.note: to bank something is to hold it safe inside, so the first word holds the second

parts.note: pathetically means in a pitiful, sad way

indicators.note: most of the word drops its final letter

parts.note: rent is a payment made to a landlord

explanation.surface: Someone sadly depositing most of their pay.
explanation.walkthrough: 'banking' suggests money, which suits the payment; here it means holding inside. The definition shows its own sense: the bracketed words are an aside.
explanation.definitionFit: The words in brackets are set aside in the manner of a bracketed remark, an aside.

clue.text: Good deal for item to be sold

definitions.meaning: something put up at an auction under a number

explanation.surface: A bargain on something going under the hammer.
explanation.definitionFit: A word for a great quantity, and also each article or bundle offered at an auction.

clue.text: Hard — of hearing?

definitions.meaning: difficult and wearing to deal with
describing a court hearing, where a judge sits to judge a case

explanation.surface: Hard of hearing, deaf.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Hard of hearing' reads as deafness, but it splits into two meanings: difficult, and conducting a court hearing.
explanation.definitionFit: Exhausting to endure means difficult, while a judge hearing a case is conducting a trial.

clue.text: Bill collecting £50 for surveyor

indicators.note: the poster collects, takes in, the two letters

parts.note: a bill is a poster stuck on a wall
L, from the Latin libra, is the symbol for a pound
L is the Roman numeral for fifty

explanation.surface: A bill that includes a fifty-pound charge for a surveyor.
explanation.walkthrough: '£50' gives two pieces: L for the pound sign and L for fifty.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who conducts opinion polls is surveying the public, a surveyor of views.
